4fFDFbi3toc.summary: Will Wilson of FoundationDB explains how the team tested their distributed database using deterministic simulation. By running the whole system in a simulator with injected faults and reproducible seeds, they could find rare concurrency and network bugs.
4fFDFbi3toc.why: HN treats it as the canonical talk on simulation testing and a mind-blowing example of how far rigorous testing can go.

4Q7FTjhvZ7Y.summary: Code Rush is a one-hour documentary following Netscape engineers in Silicon Valley through the company's last year as an independent firm. It covers the Mozilla open-source announcement, the frantic push to ready the source for release by March 31, 1998, and the toll on engineers' lives before the AOL acquisition.
4Q7FTjhvZ7Y.why: HN commenters recommend it as an intimate, embedded look at late-90s web history and the spirit of building something important under pressure.

4Z2uzEM0ugY.summary: Christopher Hitchens delivers a speech defending freedom of speech, including the right of audiences to hear offensive speakers and a take on the fire-in-a-crowded-theatre line. It is framed around the Charlie Hebdo attack.
4Z2uzEM0ugY.why: HN invokes it in nearly every content moderation and censorship thread as the most eloquent case for free speech.

4XpnKHJAok8.summary: Linus Torvalds gives a Google tech talk on git, the source control system he created two years earlier. He argues for distributed version control over centralized systems such as CVS and Subversion.
4XpnKHJAok8.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as the iconic explanation of why git is designed as it is and why distributed VCS beats centralized ones.

42QuXLucH3Q.summary: Veritasium explains why a large share of published research findings may be false, covering p-values, p-hacking, publication bias and low replication rates. It draws on John Ioannidis's well-known paper and describes reforms such as preregistration.
42QuXLucH3Q.why: HN commenters link it whenever a shaky study or the p<0.05 threshold comes up, as a short primer on false positives in science.

443UNeGrFoM.summary: Eskil Steenberg's two-hour talk on his personal approach to writing C, covering code style, structure, naming, pointers and large-project organization. He warns it contains a fair bit of programming religion.
443UNeGrFoM.why: HN recommends it as the one long programming video worth watching, a provocative and influential take on C.

4PaWFYm0kEw.summary: Bryan Cantrill's Monktoberfest 2016 talk on how software engineers pass knowledge down through oral tradition, from folk rhymes to programmer lore and stories like why C lacks a logical XOR. He argues for writing software with future generations in mind.
4PaWFYm0kEw.why: HN recommends it as an entertaining, well-delivered talk full of stories that shows the value of historical context and long comments in code.

4bM3Gut1hIk.summary: Christopher Domas presents his Cantor Dust tool at Derbycon 2012, a 3D visual approach to reverse engineering binaries by visualizing their structure dynamically.
4bM3Gut1hIk.why: Regarded as one of the coolest talks ever, with a futuristic binary visualization demo that has inspired later tools.

4d0EGIt1SPc.summary: PBS Space Time explains the proposal to use the Sun's gravity as a giant lens, sending a train of small light-sail spacecraft to the focal point roughly 550 AU out. It covers how such a telescope could image exoplanets in surprising detail and the engineering challenges involved.
4d0EGIt1SPc.why: It is the go-to explanation whenever a thread touches on imaging exoplanets or solar gravitational lens telescopes.

43XKfuptnik.summary: Technology Connections' long closing video in his heat pump series, arguing that adopting heat pumps is well within reach. It explains how they work and what it takes to start using them.
43XKfuptnik.why: HN recommends the series as an enthusiastic, entertaining deep dive into residential heat pumps whenever heating or climate threads arise.

43XaZEn2aLc.summary: Shriram Krishnamurthi's PWLConf 2019 talk on the formal notion of expressive power of programming languages, based on Felleisen's paper. It explains how to tell when a feature adds power by whether emulating it requires global rewriting.
43XaZEn2aLc.why: Recommended as the approachable way into a precise definition of language expressiveness for language-design arguments.

4nigRT2KmCE.summary: MC Frontalot's nerdcore rap about the text adventure Zork, made for Jason Scott's Get Lamp documentary and featuring a cameo by Steve Meretzky. It was filmed over an evening in a basement.
4nigRT2KmCE.why: HN shares it whenever Zork or text adventures come up, as a fun tribute for geeks.

48sCx-wBs34.summary: Veritasium explains how Penrose tilings and quasicrystals overturned the belief that 5-fold symmetry and non-periodic crystals were impossible, including an interview with Paul Steinhardt.
48sCx-wBs34.why: Strongly recommended as a mind-bending, approachable explanation of aperiodic patterns, even enjoyable with kids.

4bZvq3nodf4.summary: Alex Russell's Chrome Dev Summit 2016 talk on building web experiences that work on slow, flaky networks and low-power devices. It argues developers should focus on the performance of real-world mobile hardware rather than desktop machines.
4bZvq3nodf4.why: HN commenters cite it as the clearest case for why mobile devices are slow and why code-splitting and progressive web apps are needed.

41VJudBdYXY.summary: A Bloomberg mini-documentary on how Vienna keeps housing affordable through large-scale public and social housing. It presents the city as a model strategy for others.
41VJudBdYXY.why: HN points to it in housing-cost threads as the standard example of government-built housing keeping rents down.

449j7oKQVkc.summary: Ron Pressler's Curry On 2015 talk arguing that imperative languages should not be polluted with pure functional concepts like monads. He favors simple blocking code over non-blocking styles.
449j7oKQVkc.why: Recommended as the case for blocking code and virtual threads over monads and async/await.

4RSht_aV7AU.summary: David Beazley's PyData Global 2021 keynote, an oral history of early scientific Python. He tells how Python ended up running on a Connection Machine supercomputer at Los Alamos.
4RSht_aV7AU.why: Cited in threads about Python's rise as a first-hand, entertaining account of why it won in scientific computing.

4hZxo96x48A.summary: Tantacrul gives a detailed UX and UI design review of the MuseScore 3 notation software and compares it with Sibelius. It examines visual appeal, navigation and notation quality.
4hZxo96x48A.why: Cited as a funny, informative teardown of bad interface design, and for the story that MuseScore hired him as head of design afterward.

4oAB83Z1ydE.summary: Apple's classic 'Think Different' commercial, a one-minute spot celebrating creative misfits and innovators. This upload is from 2006.
4oAB83Z1ydE.why: Shared as an emotionally powerful example of great advertising, especially after Steve Jobs died.

4-SGpEInX_c.summary: A long Lex Fridman interview with Stephen Wolfram on complexity, cellular automata, computational irreducibility and the Wolfram Physics Project.
4-SGpEInX_c.why: HN recommends it as an accessible way into Wolfram's physics ideas and his personality.

42oQN7fy_eM.summary: Not Just Bikes argues that stop signs are a poor traffic control, drawing on Dutch practice and the Idaho stop to show intersections can be safer without them, especially for cyclists.
42oQN7fy_eM.why: Cited in threads about cyclist safety and traffic law as an explanation of why removing stop signs can improve safety.

43CMV8KIs3E.summary: Hoeg Law's Virtual Legality walks through the 185-page Epic v. Apple decision, covering antitrust law, relevant markets, anti-steering and who actually won. It runs well over two hours and corrects common media misreadings.
43CMV8KIs3E.why: Strongly recommended as the best explanation of the ruling, in more depth and with more accuracy than press coverage.

495nCzxM9PI.summary: Earliest known footage of Ivan Sutherland's MIT PhD work, Sketchpad, the first computer graphics system, with commentary by Alan Kay. It shows light-pen drawing with constraints in a short clip.
495nCzxM9PI.why: HN points people to it as the canonical demo of early interactive graphics, constraints and objects, and as one of Alan Kay's favorite things to show.

4AC6RSau7r8.summary: Paul Grignon's animated documentary presenting his view of how banks create money as debt and why that system requires continuous growth. It outlines the historical background of modern banking.
4AC6RSau7r8.why: Recommended as an approachable explanation of fractional reserve banking, with the caveat that it is biased.

4P_kbF0EbZM.summary: Stephan T. Lavavej's CppCon 2019 talk on implementing floating-point to_chars and from_chars in Microsoft's C++ STL. It covers the history of float-string conversion and the algorithms that make it much faster.
4P_kbF0EbZM.why: HN calls it a surprisingly fun, approachable talk on a hard problem and cites it in floating-point threads.

4QXZ2RzN_Oo.summary: Scott Manley explains the plumbing of rocket engines, including pressure-fed, gas generator, expander and staged combustion cycles. He shows why more complex designs exist and what they gain.
4QXZ2RzN_Oo.why: Recommended whenever rocket engine cycles or turbopumps come up, as a clear introduction from a trusted explainer.

4aw9uyj9MAE.summary: GDC 2019 session where Insomniac's David Santiago describes the procedural systems used to build Manhattan for Marvel's Spider-Man. It covers the open-world pipeline and how each system was designed to support iteration and dependencies.
4aw9uyj9MAE.why: Recommended as a prime example of large-scale procedural generation used in a shipped AAA game.

4s9IjkMAmns.summary: A lightning-style conference talk by Ricardo Signes about the horrors of email: its protocols, formats and decades of accumulated quirks. It is delivered with a humorous horror theme to show why handling email correctly is harder than it looks.
4s9IjkMAmns.why: HN points to it whenever someone underestimates how hard email parsing, validation or building a mail client really is.

4zgYG-_ha28.summary: John Carmack's keynote at QuakeCon 2011, an hour and a half of wide-ranging talk about id Software, Rage, engine open-sourcing, patents and programming practices.
4zgYG-_ha28.why: Cited as a source for Carmack's views on static analysis, open source and languages, and praised as a captivating, conversational speaker.

46ehrFk-gLk.summary: Tom Scott argues that grammatical gender is a silly concept and that the singular 'they' is an established gender-neutral pronoun. The description carries later corrections and reflections he added in 2019.
46ehrFk-gLk.why: HN commenters link it as a short, friendly explanation of singular they and grammatical gender in discussions of pronoun usage.

4AfRAVcThyA.summary: At CppCon 2017 Herb Sutter presents his work on evolving C++ through compile-time code generation, including metaclasses and reflection. The aim is to make the language both more powerful and simpler by letting programmers express intent directly.
4AfRAVcThyA.why: Praised as the best talk of CppCon 2017 and the key introduction to metaclasses and generative C++.

4F72VULWFvc.summary: Misko Hevery's Clean Code Talk shows how to use object-oriented techniques such as polymorphism to remove repeated if and switch statements. The result is code that is easier to test, understand and maintain.
4F72VULWFvc.why: HN commenters recommend it as a thorough treatment of replacing conditionals with polymorphism and why flags and deep ifs can be code smells.

4HgShra-KnY.summary: Chris Lattner's ASPLOS 2021 keynote on the golden age of compiler design in an era of hardware and software co-design, covering compiler infrastructure for accelerators and unifying hardware IRs.
4HgShra-KnY.why: Recommended for explaining where the compiler ecosystem lacks standardization for accelerators and why efforts like MLIR and CIRCT matter.

4YYvBLAF4T8.summary: Deviant Ollam shows that most physical attacks on doors bypass the lock, with photo and video examples of how doors, frames and hardware get defeated. It is a physical security talk from Shakacon.
4YYvBLAF4T8.why: HN recommends it as an interesting talk on how weak real-world door security is, and cites it for the stories of bad doors.

4t1K66dMhWk.summary: Jonathan Blow's hour-long livestreamed response to a RustConf 2018 closing keynote about entity systems in Rust. He argues that index-based entity systems amount to manual memory management that sidesteps the borrow checker, and he talks about friction for game developers.
4t1K66dMhWk.why: It is the standard citation in HN arguments over Rust for game development, the borrow checker and ECS designs, as a skeptical view from an experienced game developer.

4xGawJIseNY.summary: The introduction to Innuendo Studios' video essay series on the rhetorical tactics of the alt-right. It examines how bad-faith debate and harassment work online.
4xGawJIseNY.why: Recommended as a primer on recognising trolling and dog-whistle tactics in online discussion.

45mMioJ5szc.summary: A Nike commercial in which Michael Jordan lists the shots he missed and games he lost, saying that repeated failure is the reason he succeeds.
45mMioJ5szc.why: HN invokes it as the classic illustration of learning through repeated failure and iterating, often in startup threads.

4JWwOzEDGss.summary: A Sesame Street animation from 1979 with music composed by Philip Glass, showing geometric circle patterns.
4JWwOzEDGss.why: Mentioned as an example of Sesame Street respecting children's intelligence and as an early gateway to modern classical music.

4VrLQXR7mKU.summary: Victoria Warmerdam's Oscar-winning Dutch short film in which a woman fails a series of Captcha tests and is plunged into a strange new reality. It is a dark, Black Mirror-like sci-fi comedy.
4VrLQXR7mKU.why: HN brings it up in threads about captchas, bots and AI agents as an excellent short film about being a robot.

4YTfxresvS8.summary: Raph Levien presents his new Rust GUI framework, built on data-oriented design and ideas from entity component systems, for the Xi editor. He weighs the approach against alternatives and discusses pros and cons.
4YTfxresvS8.why: HN people point to it as an excellent, inspirational talk on Rust GUI architecture, and it led many to the Druid project.

4kLPyV8lBbs.summary: A Berkeley lecture by psychologist Christina Maslach, a leading burnout researcher, on what burnout is and what causes it. It covers common misunderstandings and the job and workplace factors involved.
4kLPyV8lBbs.why: HN uses it as the expert primer on burnout that dispels common misconceptions.

4q1dgn_C0AU.summary: Psychologist Dan Gilbert argues in this TED talk that our psychological immune system lets us become happy even when things do not go as planned. He challenges the idea that we will be miserable if we do not get what we want.
4q1dgn_C0AU.why: HN cites it as one of the best TED talks and as evidence that people adapt to and come to like outcomes they cannot change.

45X4VP8CGtk.summary: Connor Krukosky, an 18-year-old college student and vintage computer collector, tells how he bought an IBM z890 mainframe and got it running at home. The talk was given at SHARE in San Antonio in March 2016.
45X4VP8CGtk.why: HN commenters cite it as an entertaining example of a teenager buying, hosting and booting a real mainframe.

49kBWM3RQQ8.summary: The first episode of Mike Zamansky's Using Emacs series, covering setting up the package manager for new Emacs users as a start toward customization and efficient editing.
49kBWM3RQQ8.why: Recommended as a practical, step-by-step video path for learning Emacs.

4KtotxNAwME.summary: Leptos creator Greg Johnston examines Rust/WebAssembly frontend frameworks against JavaScript frameworks using the JS framework benchmark. He argues that WASM is no longer too slow for DOM-heavy rendering.
4KtotxNAwME.why: Cited as evidence that DOM access is not the bottleneck for WebAssembly, and as an explanation of signals-based updates versus virtual DOM.

4KuVvb9DTaU.summary: Louis Rossmann discusses failing keyboards on newer MacBooks, comparing a Dell keyboard repair with an Apple keyboard repair and explaining why Apple's design is costly and hard to fix.
4KuVvb9DTaU.why: Cited in MacBook keyboard and repairability threads for its clear teardown of what a replacement involves.

4PHT-zBxKQQ.summary: People Make Games explores VRChat, the social virtual world that many consider the metaverse people actually like, interviewing users and covering its communities and uncertain future.
4PHT-zBxKQQ.why: Recommended as a mini documentary that explains VRChat's culture and contrasts it with Meta's Horizon Worlds.

4Vw6uF2LdZw.summary: Hillsdale historian Burt Folsom lectures at a 2011 seminar on the 'robber barons' of the Gilded Age. He argues that figures like Vanderbilt and Rockefeller were market entrepreneurs rather than monopolists.
4Vw6uF2LdZw.why: HN people offer it as a free-market counterpoint to the standard robber baron narrative.

4WwAQqWUkpI.summary: Robert Sapolsky's Stanford lecture on the biological underpinnings of religiosity, from his human behavioral biology course. It covers theories linking religion to stress, and schizotypal traits.
4WwAQqWUkpI.why: Recommended when religion, mental health or psychedelics come up, for Sapolsky's biological framing.

4_qJptwikRc.summary: Sabine Hossenfelder explains how her opinion on dark matter has shifted, weighing the evidence for and against it and the case for modified gravity. It runs through what dark matter is and why it has not been detected.
4_qJptwikRc.why: Recommended as an accessible, curious-undergraduate-level overview of dark matter and its alternatives.

4aUODXeAM-k.summary: Kyle Hill explains what nuclear waste actually is and how it is stored, arguing that the problem was effectively solved decades ago. It covers solid shielded waste and deep geological storage.
4aUODXeAM-k.why: Cited in nuclear power debates to argue that waste storage is a political rather than technical problem.

4anAwXYqLG8.summary: Sebastian Markbage explains how React is moving toward a minimal API surface by leaning on language features and patterns instead of dedicated framework APIs. He also touches on JSX and syntax proposals for future JavaScript.
4anAwXYqLG8.why: HN cites it as a statement of React's early design philosophy of keeping APIs small and understanding JavaScript itself.

4jEz03Z8azc.summary: Sped-up onboard camera footage of the Falcon 9 first stage landing on a drone ship during the THAICOM 8 mission on May 27, 2016. It shows the descent from grid fin deployment to touchdown.
4jEz03Z8azc.why: HN links it in SpaceX landing threads as the best first-person view of how hard a booster landing is.

4j_UjIshzMc.summary: Builders Matt Risinger and Jordan Smith visit a Swiss cross-laminated timber factory that makes thick all-wood walls with no traditional insulation and wooden nails instead of glue or chemicals. The video is sponsored by Siga.
4j_UjIshzMc.why: HN cites it in mass timber and construction threads as an example of insulation-free, glue-free all-wood building in Europe.

4jh94gowim0.summary: Paul Phillips, a major Scala compiler contributor, gives a long talk on Scala collections and views, using it to critique Scala's design and direction.
4jh94gowim0.why: Cited in Scala debates as an insider's critique that persuaded many the language's problems were deep.

4moyKUHApq4.summary: Sean Parent of Adobe argues that object-oriented frameworks ultimately fail to deliver scalable, high quality software and proposes combining generic and declarative programming instead. It draws on Stepanov's Elements of Programming.
4moyKUHApq4.why: Frequently cited for the claim that Photoshop's codebase could shrink dramatically with generic programming.

4zG0uecYSMA.summary: A 1990 lecture by James Gosling on NeWS, Sun's networked window system in which clients send PostScript programs to the server for execution. It covers the high-level imaging model and compares NeWS with similar systems.
4zG0uecYSMA.why: Shared in threads on window systems and X11 history as a primary-source talk on why NeWS was technically ahead of X.

4S9sDyooxf4.summary: Sabine Hossenfelder explains climate sensitivity and why recent observations suggest climate models may have underestimated warming. She says this changed her view on how worried to be.
4S9sDyooxf4.why: HN commenters link it as the direct source on climate sensitivity and on the claim that past models ran too cold.

4To-F6W1NT0.summary: Louis Rossmann explains why he stopped using GrapheneOS, describing his interactions with its lead developer Daniel Micay. It includes chat logs shown in the video.
4To-F6W1NT0.why: HN uses it as the key reference in arguments about Micay's conduct and GrapheneOS leadership, with some defending it and some urging skepticism.

4Tr0otuiQuU.summary: A full piano performance of Beethoven's Piano Sonata No. 14, the Moonlight Sonata, with all three movements: Adagio sostenuto, Allegretto and Presto agitato.
4Tr0otuiQuU.why: Mostly cited as an example piece in audio and AI-music discussions, with one commenter urging people to hear the whole sonata, especially the third movement.

4Z75A_JMBx4.summary: Farmer Joel Salatin gives a TEDx talk on how well-managed grass and rotational grazing support sustainable farming and affect the climate. He draws on his work at Polyface Farm in Virginia.
4Z75A_JMBx4.why: HN cites it in climate and diet debates as a contrarian perspective that cattle on managed pasture can be part of the solution.

4rTv9wvvat8.summary: ScienceClic visualizes what you would see falling into a black hole, from the approach and the accretion disc to crossing the horizon, in 15 minutes.
4rTv9wvvat8.why: Recommended as a great visual explanation of the infall experience, including when spaghettification happens.

4-oV42OMQoE.summary: A ten-minute clip of Noam Chomsky on the Faurisson affair and free speech. He argues that supporting free speech means defending views you despise.
4-oV42OMQoE.why: HN quotes it in censorship and moderation threads for Chomsky's principle that free speech must cover speech you dislike.

469chceiiUQ.summary: PBS Space Time considers whether life could be based on silicon instead of carbon, comparing the two elements' chemistry and why silicon is the most plausible alternative.
469chceiiUQ.why: Recommended as a solid, informative treatment of silicon-based life and the chemical limits on alien biochemistry.

480xteW2wq4.summary: A short demo of typing on the Modos Paper Monitor, an open e-ink monitor, using 4-level grayscale to show low latency.
480xteW2wq4.why: Pointed to as evidence that open e-ink controllers can reach usable latency for real computer use.

4AivEQmfPpk.summary: A short CGP Grey explainer about how countries are defined, why recognition by others matters, and the oddities of places like Taiwan and Vatican City. It shows that statehood is partly a matter of diplomacy rather than fact.
4AivEQmfPpk.why: Cited in threads on borders, Taiwan's status and how many countries exist, as a quick explanation of why recognition is political.

4DKrcpa8Z_E.summary: A short Insider Tech look at Ocado's grocery warehouse where thousands of robots on a grid pack orders, communicating over 4G to avoid collisions. It handles around 65,000 orders a week.
4DKrcpa8Z_E.why: HN cites it as the standard example of advanced warehouse automation in grocery fulfillment.

4G_1uy_7B5w.summary: LGR looks at the 1988 Canon Xap Shot, a still video camera that records photos to a floppy disk as analog NTSC signal rather than digital data.
4G_1uy_7B5w.why: HN shares it as a fun explanation of analog floppy-disk cameras.

4JuoOaL11bw.summary: Google engineer Dany Qumsiyeh presents a prototype automatic, non-destructive book scanner that turns pages and captures high-resolution images, built in Google's workshops. The talk includes a live demo and a short technical overview.
4JuoOaL11bw.why: HN cites it as the example of Google's open-sourced linear book scanner design when discussing book digitization.

4K5fbQ1-zps.summary: A short animated explainer that stages a $100 footrace in which contestants start at different distances from the line, depending on the advantages or disadvantages they inherited. It uses the race as a metaphor for how unequal starting points shape outcomes, citing US census income and poverty figures.
4K5fbQ1-zps.why: HN commenters link it as a quick, memorable illustration of unequal starting positions and generational wealth in threads on personal finance and economic precarity.

4LqZdkkBDas.summary: ContraPoints' long-form video response to Jordan Peterson, critiquing his ideas including his use of the term postmodern neo-Marxism. It is delivered in her theatrical essay style.
4LqZdkkBDas.why: HN mostly cites it as the go-to critique of Peterson when his positions or advice come up.

4Q_mY54hjM0.summary: Philosopher Daniel Dennett visits Google to discuss his book Intuition Pumps and Other Tools for Thinking, describing thought experiments and thinking tools across psychology, biology, computer science and physics.
4Q_mY54hjM0.why: Pointed to as an accessible introduction to intuition pumps as thinking tools, and shared in remembrance after Dennett's death.

4VKZTmTP7oY.summary: Naomi Wu documents her project helping Martha Lillard, one of the last polio survivors living in an iron lung, by fabricating replacement neck collars in Shenzhen. She reports the collars worked.
4VKZTmTP7oY.why: HN cites it as a concrete example of a maker helping save someone's life, and as evidence of Wu's work when she was omitted from press coverage.

4WO5kJChg3w.summary: Y Combinator's Geoff Ralston interviews Paul Graham about startups and founders in a Startup School conversation. It touches on Viaweb, Robert Morris and what makes founders effective.
4WO5kJChg3w.why: HN mostly cites it for specific Graham remarks, such as advice to find a paying customer and a recent interview about Viaweb.

4Wrc4fHSCpw.summary: A Veritasium video on the asteroid threat, with UCLA's Dave Jewitt explaining detection efforts and how different asteroid sizes compare in damage.
4Wrc4fHSCpw.why: HN cites it in asteroid threads for how well-tracked large asteroids are and how hard deflection is.

4eRCygdW--c.summary: A recording of Richard Feynman's talk on the possibilities of manipulating matter at very small scales, widely seen as an early vision of nanotechnology. This is a later version of his 1959 "There's Plenty of Room at the Bottom" lecture.
4eRCygdW--c.why: HN points to it when discussing nanobots and microscale physics, including how things behave at tiny scales.

4kpDg7MjHps.summary: A June 1986 CNN interview with physicist Richard Feynman about the Challenger disaster and the management failures he found while serving on the investigating commission.
4kpDg7MjHps.why: HN cites it for Feynman's insights on NASA risk reasoning, blame and engineering culture, and the contrast between Apollo and the Shuttle.

4lmW2tZP2kU.summary: A 54-second clip from the film Office Space in which two coworkers talk about what they would do with a million dollars. The answers contrast blue-collar and white-collar attitudes toward work.
4lmW2tZP2kU.why: Mostly a joke reference in threads about layoffs, idleness and wealth, with one commenter sincerely recommending the clip for its contrast of work attitudes.

4loZGYqaZ7I.summary: The fail0verflow 27C3 talk on breaking PS3 security, covering how Sony's implementation failed, including its ECDSA mistakes.
4loZGYqaZ7I.why: Recommended as a fun, detailed account of how the PS3's security was broken.

4y43qwS8fl4.summary: Jeff Hawkins presents his view that the neocortex works on principles different from traditional computers. He describes sparse distributed representations and how they are learned, then shows how Numenta applies them to predict from high-velocity data streams.
4y43qwS8fl4.why: Recommended as Hawkins' own accessible statement of his brain-inspired theory of intelligence and its software implementation.

41XgkLKYuic.summary: Valve News Network goes through over twenty accounts from ex-Valve employees, mostly from Glassdoor, about what it is like to work at Valve. It covers the company's flat structure and culture.
41XgkLKYuic.why: HN commenters cite it as a summary of former employees' experience that the flat structure produces informal hierarchy, cliques and stack ranking.

4NAzQPll7Lo.summary: Rap Genius founders appear at TechCrunch Disrupt NY 2013 for a joke-filled interview announcing News Genius, with little detail about what it is.
4NAzQPll7Lo.why: HN mostly cites it as an example of the founders' brash, unprofessional behavior, not as something to watch.

4QokOwvPxrE.summary: A short screen recording of an Ubuntu Karmic Koala desktop running KDE4 with Compiz Fusion 3D cube effects and CairoDock.
4QokOwvPxrE.why: HN cites it as an example of 3D desktop eye candy that was famous and popular, and of how effects can be overdone.

4TxkE_oYrjU.summary: Thunderf00t's critique of SpaceX's claims, arguing its launches are not actually cheaper than competitors or the Space Shuttle. It questions the economics of reusability.
4TxkE_oYrjU.why: HN commenters cite it as the skeptical case against SpaceX's cost claims, mostly in critical arguments rather than as a recommendation.

4U2eDJnwz_s.summary: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on auto lending, showing how lenders steer vulnerable buyers into subprime loans and crushing debt. It uses comedy sketches to explain the practices.
4U2eDJnwz_s.why: Cited for subprime auto loan statistics and as a reference for predatory car financing, rather than as a recommendation.

4ZK8Z8hulFg.summary: A one-minute ProZD comedy sketch about how a person's enthusiasm for a hobby changes after they discover its subreddit. It satirizes how communities turn casual interest into gatekeeping and gear obsession.
4ZK8Z8hulFg.why: Used as a joke when HN threads show enthusiasts arguing over niche details.

4dn6ZVpJLxs.summary: A long, sarcastic critique of Elon Musk's Loop tunnel transit idea and related Boring Company and Hyperloop claims. It leans on transit-planning arguments about capacity and throughput.
4dn6ZVpJLxs.why: HN uses it as the go-to rebuttal when Musk's transportation proposals come up, though it is mostly cited by skeptics.

4eFD_Wj6dhk.summary: A GoPro-recorded flight of an RC glider setting a 548 mph dynamic soaring speed record at Parker Mountain, California, using only wind gradients.
4eFD_Wj6dhk.why: Cited as a striking example of dynamic soaring letting unpowered gliders far exceed wind speed.

4iFYaeoE3n4.summary: A one-minute clip of Madeleine Albright on 60 Minutes, answering a question about the cost of sanctions on Iraq.
4iFYaeoE3n4.why: Linked as a critical example of official indifference to civilian costs of foreign policy.

4pS4x8hXQ5c.summary: A Vox Strikethrough video arguing that CNN models its political coverage on sports shows like First Take, pitting pundits against each other. It claims this favors drama over truth and degrades public understanding.
4pS4x8hXQ5c.why: Cited as an example of how cable news turns politics into sports-style controversy, not recommended much as a watch.

4pbAI40dK0A.summary: A short research demo of Autonomous Intersection Management, a protocol in which self-driving cars reserve slots through an intersection instead of obeying signals or stop signs.
